[ For apps ]

Reach users on Ethereum mainnet and every EEZ chain verified with yours.

Deploy once. Users on the other chains call your contract in one transaction, and it lands whole or not at all.

What you can build

Name lookup on L1

Resolve a name on mainnet and use the address inside your transaction.

Unified liquidity

Pools stay on their own chains; one order fills from all of them in the same transaction.

Atomic arbitrage

Buy on one chain, sell on another, in one transaction. You keep the margin.

All use cases →

What it takes

0changes to your L1 contractsThey stay as they are. Cross-chain callers reach them through a proxy.
1proxy per contract you callA stand-in address on your chain. Anyone can create one, on the plain RPC.
1endpoint for cross-chain callsSend them to the composer. Plain transactions keep using your RPC.

Before you commit

What changes for your contract.
vs
What you get

Live

  • The call lands or reverts whole within one L1 block
  • Standard RPC, logs and receipts
Plan for these

What changes

  • msg.sender is the proxy: allowlist the proxy, not the user
  • Each cross-chain call sets its own destination gas
  • Rollup-to-rollup calls work between rollups verified in the same L1 block
How a call works, step by step

Which contract, which chain

Answer three questions and the scoper tells you whether your pattern works today, with changes, or not yet.
